prerequisites: Fundamentos Químicos de la Ingeniería (Chemical Engineering Fundamentals)

learning_outcomes.text: Basic knowledge and application of environmental and sustainability technologies.

That students have demonstrated possession and understanding of knowledge in a field of study that builds on general secondary education, and is usually at a level that, although supported by advanced textbooks, also includes some aspects that imply knowledge from the forefront of their field of study.

That students know how to apply their knowledge to their work or vocation in a professional way and possess the competencies that are usually demonstrated by the elaboration and defense of arguments and the resolution of problems within their area of study.

That students have the ability to collect and interpret relevant data (usually within their field of study) to make judgments that include a reflection on relevant social, scientific or ethical issues.
Ability to work in a multilingual and multidisciplinary environment.
Knowledge in basic and technological subjects, which enables them to learn new methods and theories, and provides them with versatility to adapt to new situations.
Ability to solve problems with initiative, decision-making, creativity, critical reasoning and to communicate and transmit knowledge, skills and abilities in the field of Industrial Engineering.
Knowledge for carrying out measurements, calculations, valuations, appraisals, expert reports, studies, reports, work plans and other similar tasks.
Ability to manage specifications, regulations and mandatory standards.
Project aptitudes in engineering in the fields of application of the subject.

syllabus_topics: Topic 2: Environmental conservation. Main environmental problems.
Topic 6: The atmosphere and atmospheric pollutants.
Topic 11: Conditions for emission of pollutants to the atmosphere and water.
teaching_methods: Distance virtualized course via UNED-e virtual learning portal and Ágora e-Learning platform.
Communication through virtual course forums and email.
Communication through educational technical and communication resources (e.g., radio/TV programs, presentations, conferences in digital repositories).
assessment_rules: The face-to-face exam (PP) consists of four conceptual or practical questions (6 points) and one problem (4 points), lasts 120 minutes, and allows a non-programmable calculator. A minimum score of 5 on the PP is required to pass without continuous assessment (PEC/AE), or 4 points to add the PEC/AE scores. PEC and AE are optional and can each add up to 0.5 points to the final grade. Mandatory laboratory practices must be successfully completed after passing the exam, for both February and September calls.
